html:
SMTO-SKL-0049 — SMTO couldn't confirm whether your Drive change happened

GUID: ae101c9d-330f-5d18-a87f-bdbfabea3dc3
Slug: google-drive-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • SMTO sent a change to Google Drive but didn't get a clear answer back, and it couldn't confirm the result afterward. The change may or may not have been made.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: open Google Drive and look for the result, such as the uploaded file, new folder, copy, new name or location, or a removed file. Google may have made the change even though SMTO didn't get confirmation.
  2. If you see two copies of an uploaded or copied file, keep the complete one and delete only the extra. This leaves one correct copy without losing the original.
  3. Only if the change is definitely not there, ask SMTO to do it again and approve the request. Repeating a change that already happened can create duplicates or overwrite newer work.

What success looks like

  • Google Drive shows the change exactly once, as you intended.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the details identify the file or operation to check. Don't ask SMTO to repeat the change until you've checked Drive.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Drive mutation outcome is unknown: a transport or server failure, unsafe session URL, ambiguous correlation lookup, inconsistent upload offset, or unverifiable returned identity/size/checksum left the write result unconfirmed, and SMTO's correlation or re-read check (where the operation supports one) could not settle it.

What this means

  • Drive cannot establish a reliable write result because of transport/server failure, unsafe returned session URL, ambiguous correlation, inconsistent upload offsets or unverifiable returned identity/size/checksum. The provider may already have applied the mutation. Inspect the exact retained resource/correlation and reconcile its state before issuing another write; the diagnostic never retries it.

Why this can happen

  • Drive cannot establish a reliable write result because of transport/server failure, unsafe returned session URL, ambiguous correlation, inconsistent upload offsets or unverifiable returned identity/size/checksum.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained file ID or smto_operation correlation and transfer acknowledgement.

How to fix it

  • Do not repeat the mutation. Inspect the exact file_id or the file carrying appProperties smto_operation equal to the reported correlation_id (google_drive.info / google_drive.search) and compare name, parents, size and checksum before issuing another write; SMTO does not retry this automatically.
  • Do not repeat the mutation. Inspect the exact file ID or smto_operation correlation before another write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not repeat the mutation. Inspect the exact file ID or smto_operation correlation before another write.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact remote object and its content are reconciled before another write.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • The provider may already have applied the mutation. Inspect the exact retained resource/correlation and reconcile its state before issuing another write; the diagnostic never retries it.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
